thread:
maria: heads up — during the eu canary cutover ~10:30 UTC we observed the canary getting ~3% of traffic instead of the configured 10%. noticed right after the helm release flip.
aj: wait, 3%? that's... odd. which component is doing the split? istio or our split-operator?
sasha: split-operator (gitops) should be handling the weights. i'm pulling logs from the routing-controller.
deploy-bot: deployment/redwood-api v2.14.0 -> v2.15.0 triggered by pipeline #5821 (gitops)
maria: quick summary of what we saw: routing-controller applied the new Split CR, but envoy access logs show requests still hitting baseline hosts disproportionately. also saw a few canary pods Pending in eu-west-1b — taint mismatch on the gpu nodepool?
luca-oncall: oncall jump in. can you paste the split CR and the svc/ingress config?
sasha: here's the split we applied:
```yaml
apiVersion: traffic.redwood.io/v1
kind: Split
metadata:
  name: redwood-api-canary
spec:
  service: redwood-api
  backends:
    - name: baseline
      weight: 90
    - name: canary
      weight: 10
```
aj: looks fine. what do pod counts look like on canary?
maria: current replica set shows 4/6 canary pods Ready, baseline 24/24. The two pending pods are stuck on taints: `gpu-reserved:NoSchedule` — gitops changed nodeSelector for canary to `nodepool:gpu-burst` but that pool has different taints in eu-west-1b.
sasha: ah that explains some of it — fewer canary endpoints -> load balancer hashing/round robin will naturally bias. but 3% still low even for 4 pods. suspecting ingress host-level traffic apportioning plus per-host rounding.
aj: we have a known issue where the routing-controller apportions weights per active backend host, rounding down on small host counts. if baseline hosts >> canary hosts per AZ, effective weight gets skewed. may need a change to apportion by request-per-second target instead.
luca-oncall: are we seeing pod restarts or OOMs that could cause transient endpoint churn?
maria: no restarts. however the two Pending pods caused the readiness check to be failing for the canary service in eu-west-1b, so loadbalancer suppressed those hosts.
sasha: immediate mitigation options:
- revert nodeSelector change in the canary chart so pods schedule to existing gpu nodepool (fast)
- scale canary replicas to match baseline pod count per AZ (ugly, will cost)
- patch routing-controller to use weighted-rps apportioning (requires rollout)
aj: given we want minimal blast radius, do a quick rollback of the chart change. I can open a hotfix now.
maria: +1, revert the nodeSelector change and re-run gitops apply. rolling back now.
deploy-bot: rollback job started: gitops/hotfix/revert-canary-nodeSelector (#5822)
sasha: also filing a ticket to make the split apportioning AZ-aware and avoid integer rounding bias for small replica counts. will include telemetry to surface effective per-AZ weight.
luca-oncall: FYI — this is why our progressive delivery automation needs a readiness gate on endpoint parity (min_active_endpoints) before traffic shift. we should add that as a config knob to the canary controller.
aj: agreed. follow-up plan: 1) rollback nodeSelector (in progress) 2) add readiness gate to split-operator to require X endpoints per backend before increasing weight 3) long-term routing-controller fix to use rps apportioning and per-AZ balancing.
maria: rollback completed and canary endpoints now 6/6 Ready. rechecking traffic distribution...
deploy-bot: canary traffic weights reconciled: baseline=90, canary=10 (applied)
maria: confirming FROM envoy logs: canary ~10.2% over last 2m. closing incident.
luca-oncall: nice work. please add postmortem note in #postmortems and link the ticket about apportioning.
sasha: filed ticket INFRA-1287 "split-operator: endpoint parity readiness gate" and INFRA-1288 "routing-controller: per-AZ rps apportioning".
aj: one last note — we should add a pre-cutover CI check that compares nodepool taints/labels referenced by chart templates vs live clusters in target regions. that would have caught the eu nodepool mismatch.
maria: good idea. will add to release checklist and open a small RFC for the preflight check. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
